title: Usage insights: pipeline lag + export job metrics (with dashboard links + alert stubs)
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Summary: Adds first-class metrics for Usage Insights (route/model) pipeline freshness/lag and export job health. This is intended to support GA gating ("data freshness is green" + "exports are reliable") and to reduce time-to-diagnosis when customers report gaps or timeouts. Details: Pipeline lag metrics: - `usage_insights_ingest_lag_seconds` (gauge): now() - newest_event_ts_seen, emitted per {env, region, deployment_mode}. - `usage_insights_metering_lag_seconds` (gauge): now() - newest_metered_usage_ts, used to explain invoice reconciliation delays. - `usage_insights_aggregate_lag_seconds` (gauge): now() - newest_hour_partition_committed, per {org_tier, region}. - `usage_insights_aggregate_job_duration_seconds` (histogram) and `usage_insights_aggregate_job_failures_total` (counter) for the hourly rollup job. Export job metrics (export svc): - `usage_insights_export_jobs_total{result}` (counter), result in {success, failed, canceled}. - `usage_insights_export_job_duration_seconds` (histogram) with stage label {queue_wait, render, compress, upload}. - `usage_insights_export_job_rows` (histogram) and `usage_insights_export_job_bytes` (histogram) for sizing/guardrail validation. - `usage_insights_export_job_timeouts_total` (counter) incremented on worker-side timeouts (distinct from user cancel). - `usage_insights_export_downloads_total` (counter) for download endpoint responses {2xx,4xx,5xx}. Notes on labels/cardinality: - No `org_id` label. All metrics are aggregated to avoid cardinality blowups. - Export metrics include `format` label (csv|json) and `time_window` label (hour|day|custom) but not free-form filters. - Pipeline lag metrics intentionally avoid `route` and `model` dimensions; those are visible in analytics queries, not metrics. Dashboards/alerts: - Adds dashboard links in the service README and stubs the alert rules in `alerts/usage_insights_rules.yml`. The alerts are conservative defaults; SRE will tune once we have real traffic. Links: - Usage insights health dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/usage-insights-health/usage-insights-health?orgId=1 - Export jobs dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/usage-insights-exports/usage-insights-exports?orgId=1 - Runbook (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.net/display/SRE/Usage+Insights+Backend+Health+Dashboards Implementation notes: - Metrics implemented in `telemetry-aggregator` and `export-jobs-worker`. - Existing tracing spans were updated to attach `export_job_id` (as an attribute only) to help correlate latency spikes; not exported as a Prom metric label. - Adds a small integration test that asserts the metrics endpoint exports the expected names (to prevent regressions during refactors). Rollout: - Safe to deploy behind existing services; no schema changes. - Alert rules are merged but not enabled by default in prod; SRE will flip in the rules repo once dashboards look stable. Related: - ENG-8430 (this PR), ENG-8425 (export service), ENG-8422 (aggregations).
commits: telemetry: emit ingest/metering lag gauges for usage-insights pipeline
aggregator: add job duration + failure counters; tag per region/env
export: add job duration histogram by stage + result counters
alerts: add usage insights rule stubs + recording rules
tests: metrics endpoint contract test + basic documentation
review_conversation:
Allison Grant (SRE): Can we avoid any labels that can silently explode? `time_window=custom` worries me if it becomes unbounded. Author (Caleb): Good call — changed `time_window` to an enum {hour, day, custom} only; it’s computed server-side from request shape, not passed through.

Nadia Rahman: For ingest lag, what are we measuring exactly? Is it "newest event seen" or "newest event fully processed"? Author: This is "newest event ts seen by the ingest consumer". I added `usage_insights_aggregate_lag_seconds` for the "fully processed" view (latest committed partition).

Mei Lin: Histogram buckets for export duration might be too coarse for large exports. Do we have >60s buckets? Author: Added buckets up to 15m and split by stage so we can see if we’re queueing vs rendering.

Kevin Osei: Please confirm we’re not exposing org/project identifiers in metrics. Author: Confirmed — no org_id/project_id labels; only env/region/deployment_mode/format/result/stage.

Allison: Alert stubs should default to disabled; we don’t want to page before tuning. Author: Added comments in rule file + ensured deployment does not auto-enable; SRE to wire in later.

Approvals: Allison Grant approved; Nadia Rahman approved; Mei Lin approved.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main. Follow-up tasks: SRE to tune thresholds and enable alerts after 1 week of beta traffic; add runbook section for common failure modes (queue saturation vs S3 upload errors).
release_notes: Internal: Added Usage Insights pipeline freshness and export job reliability metrics. Dashboards: usage-insights-health + usage-insights-exports. Alert rules added as stubs (not enabled by default).
